note: Representations below are simplified shapes of the real types at the pinned SHA, not verbatim dumps. The turn assumes foo.py is already /add'ed, edit format 'diff', model gpt-4o.

steps.narrative: The user types 'add error handling to foo.py'. Coder.run()'s while True calls get_input() (prompt_toolkit via io.get_input), then run_one() with preproc=True: slash-command check, check_for_file_mentions on the user's own text, URL detection. FileWatcher may also inject AI! comments as input.
steps.representation:
run() while True:
  user_message = get_input()
  run_one("add error handling to foo.py", preproc=True)
    → preproc_user_input: no /command, no new mentions, no URL
    → message = "add error handling to foo.py"
steps.title: Input

steps.narrative: send_message() → format_messages() → format_chat_chunks(). The wire order is fixed in ChatChunks.all_messages(): system (system prompt + examples + reminder) → examples → read-only files → repo map → done (summarized history) → chat files (full foo.py) → cur (the user message) → reminder. The repo map and chat files are injected as synthetic user/assistant pairs — fake conversation stage-managing the model. Prompt-cache breakpoints sit on the stable prefixes via add_cache_control_headers. check_tokens() asks 'Try to proceed anyway?' if over the context window; warm_cache() arms a ~5-minute keepalive thread making real max_tokens=1 calls.
steps.representation:
all_messages():
  system:    "You are an expert…" + examples + reminder
  repo:      user: <repo map> / assistant: "Ok, I won't try…"
  chat_files: user: foo.py full contents
  cur:       user: "add error handling to foo.py"
  reminder:  "…reply in SEARCH/REPLACE blocks…"
  [cache breakpoints: system/examples, repo, chat_files]
steps.title: Prompt assembly

steps.narrative: send() → Model.send_completion() → litellm.completion(model='gpt-4o', …), streaming tokens through show_send_output_stream. The call sits inside send_message()'s retry loop: exponential backoff (retry_delay *= 2 from 0.125s) up to RETRY_TIMEOUT = 60s on transient litellm errors. Context-window exhaustion is not retried; output-length truncation triggers assistant-prefill continuation. No function/tool calling — the response will be prose.
steps.representation:
Model.send_completion(messages, functions=None, stream=True)
  → litellm.completion(model="gpt-4o", messages=[…])
  → token stream: "I'll add try/except…\n```\nfoo.py\n<<<<<<< SEARCH…"
  (retry: while True, backoff ×2, give up past 60s)
steps.title: Model call

steps.narrative: EditBlockCoder.get_edits() → find_original_update_blocks(): scans the response for <<<<<<< SEARCH / ======= / >>>>>>> REPLACE fenced blocks and resolves the filename from the 3 preceding lines (exact → basename → difflib 0.8 fuzzy → any dotted name). ```bash blocks yield (None, shell_content) tuples into self.shell_commands for confirmed execution later — the model's 'run this' suggestions never execute inline. Malformed blocks raise ValueError.
steps.title: Response parsing

steps.narrative: apply_updates(): get_edits() → dry run → prepare_to_edit → apply_edits() writes the files. do_replace() tries exact match → leading-whitespace-flexible match → '...' elision (try_dotdotdots). Unmatched blocks raise ValueError with a SearchReplaceNoExactMatch report and 'did you mean' lines — that error text becomes the next reflection, not a crash. (Seam: replace_most_similar_chunk returns before replace_closest_edit_distance — the edit-distance fuzzy fallback is dead code.)
steps.representation:
apply_updates():
  edits = get_edits()            # parsed tuples
  apply_edits_dry_run(edits)     # no writes
  prepare_to_edit(edits)         # "Create new file?" if new
  apply_edits(edits)             # do_replace: exact → ws-flex → ...
→ foo.py rewritten on disk
  (no match → ValueError → reflected_message)
steps.title: Edit application

steps.narrative: auto_commit(): repo.commit(fnames=edited, context=cur_messages, aider_edits=True) — every applied turn becomes a git commit with an LLM-written message. The hash is recorded in aider_commit_hashes, which is what powers /undo. Then move_back_cur_messages() retires the turn into history and starts background summarization.
steps.representation:
auto_commit({abs/foo.py}):
  repo.commit(fnames, context=cur_messages, aider_edits=True)
  → commit a1b2c3d "Add error handling to foo.py…"
  → aider_commit_hashes.add(a1b2c3d)   # /undo reads this
  → move_back_cur_messages() → summarize_start (bg thread)
steps.title: Commit

steps.narrative: Post-apply feedback: if auto_lint, lint_edited() runs per-language lint commands; on errors aider asks 'Attempt to fix lint errors?' and, on yes, sets reflected_message = lint_errors. Then model-suggested shell blocks each require explicit per-command confirmation; then the auto_test command runs the same confirm→reflect cycle. THE SUB-LOOP: back in run_one()'s 'while message:', a set reflected_message re-prompts with the error text as a brand-new user message (re-entering at step 3), up to max_reflections = 3 — then 'Only 3 reflections allowed, stopping.' This is aider's answer to the tool-result feedback loop: errors become conversation.
steps.representation:
post-apply (:1599):
  lint_edited({foo.py}) → ["E501 line too long…"]
  confirm_ask("Attempt to fix lint errors?") → yes
  reflected_message = lint_errors

┌─ run_one() reflection sub-loop (≤3) ─────────┐
│ message = reflected_message                   │
│ → send_message(message)   [back to step 3]    │
│ → new prose → parse → apply → verify…        │
│ num_reflections: 1 → 2 → 3 → STOP             │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
steps.title: Verify & reflect

steps.narrative: Tokens streamed live via mdstream during the model call; after applying, aider prints 'Applied edit to foo.py' and — because the turn moved HEAD — the /undo hint from show_undo_hint(). Rendering is imperative throughout: there is no event stream for interfaces to subscribe to, which is why the streamlit GUI re-implements display logic instead of observing it. The REPL loop then waits for the next human input.
steps.representation:
stream:  mdstream renders tokens live
output:  "Applied edit to foo.py"
         "You can use /undo to undo and discard each aider commit."
run() while True → get_input()  # next turn
steps.title: Rendering
